assessment.subject: metallothioneins (MT-I to MT-IV)
assessment.claim_summary: Narrative review of molecular mechanisms regulating metallothionein gene expression, MTF-1 as the key trans-activator, and MT's protective role against reactive oxygen species; physiological function remains unresolved.

assessment.subject: enfuvirtide (T-20)
assessment.claim_summary: Review: enfuvirtide, a synthetic peptide binding gp41, produced a significant ~1 log10 HIV viral-load reduction vs controls at 24 weeks in two large randomized trials, with few serious adverse effects.
assessment.magnitude: ~1 log10 viral load reduction vs controls at 24 weeks

assessment.subject: investigational antiretroviral drugs
assessment.claim_summary: Review of investigational antiretroviral drugs in development (new reverse-transcriptase and protease inhibitors, entry inhibitors, integrase inhibitors) aimed at improving convenience, toxicity, and activity against resistant HIV.

assessment.subject: exenatide (AC-2993, synthetic exendin-4)
assessment.claim_summary: Company development announcement: exenatide, a GLP-1 agonist derived from Gila monster venom, entered three phase III trials for type 2 diabetes (monotherapy and combinations); no results reported.

assessment.subject: enfuvirtide
assessment.claim_summary: Review: enfuvirtide 90 mg SC twice daily plus optimised background significantly reduced plasma HIV RNA and increased CD4+ counts vs OB alone through 24-48 weeks in two randomized trials; injection-site reactions common.

assessment.subject: enfuvirtide (Fuzeon)
assessment.claim_summary: News note: FDA approved enfuvirtide in 2003 for use with other anti-HIV drugs in children 6+ and treatment-experienced adults; describes its entry-inhibitor mechanism. No study or finding reported.

assessment.subject: Sandostatin (octreotide acetate)
assessment.claim_summary: Drug profile: octreotide is used to control diarrhea and improve hypokalemia in metastatic carcinoid and VIP-secreting tumors and other conditions; side effects are generally rare and manageable with monitoring.

assessment.subject: PT-141 (peptide analog)
assessment.claim_summary: Company development announcement: Palatin is developing PT-141 nasal spray for sexual dysfunction; a phase IIb trial was completed and phase III planned. No results reported.

assessment.subject: enfuvirtide (Fuzeon, T-20)
assessment.claim_summary: Review concluding enfuvirtide, a fusion inhibitor binding gp41, showed potent antiretroviral activity in vitro/in vivo and was effective and safe in phase II/III trials, including multidrug-resistant HIV, with mild-moderate adverse effects.

assessment.subject: teriparatide (rhPTH 1-34)
assessment.claim_summary: Review: teriparatide, an anabolic PTH analog, increased BMD/BMC and reduced nonvertebral fractures (35-40% vs placebo) in postmenopausal women and men with osteoporosis; mild transient hypercalcemia observed.

assessment.subject: ziconotide
assessment.claim_summary: Review: intrathecal ziconotide, an N-type calcium-channel blocker, was significantly more effective than placebo for chronic malignant/nonmalignant pain in three trials; adverse events mostly neurological, mild-moderate and reversible.

assessment.subject: octreotide
assessment.claim_summary: Review: octreotide, a somatostatin analog, is a promising option to reduce chyle drainage in chylothorax refractory to conservative treatment, though clinical data are limited and patient response varies.

assessment.subject: beta-thymosins (thymosin beta-4)
assessment.claim_summary: Review: thymosin beta-4 is the main intracellular G-actin-sequestering peptide (micromolar Kd), evolving from a putative thymic hormone to a cytokine supporting wound healing; extracellular mechanisms remain poorly understood.

assessment.subject: thymosin beta-4 / beta-thymosins
assessment.claim_summary: Review of how thymosin beta-4 modulates actin monomer availability and cytoskeleton dynamics; its pleiotropic effects on cell motility may arise from both direct actin binding and indirect signaling.

assessment.subject: HIV entry inhibitors
assessment.claim_summary: Review of HIV entry inhibitors (fusion inhibitor enfuvirtide and coreceptor antagonists), their clinical and preclinical development, and their potential role in anti-HIV therapy.

assessment.subject: irinotecan toxicity
assessment.claim_summary: Review: irinotecan toxicity (diarrhea, neutropenia) is greater in patients with UGT1A polymorphisms and hepatic insufficiency; dose adjustment is established and 30 mg octreotide LAR adequately controls chemotherapy-induced diarrhea.

assessment.subject: degarelix (GnRH antagonist)
assessment.object: leuprolide (GnRH agonist); testosterone suppression in prostate cancer
assessment.claim_summary: Phase III RCT (n=610): degarelix was noninferior to leuprolide for maintaining testosterone <=0.5 ng/mL over 1 year (97-98% vs 96%) and suppressed testosterone and PSA faster, with more injection-site reactions.

assessment.subject: teriparatide (Forteo/Forsteo)
assessment.claim_summary: Review: subcutaneous teriparatide 20 mcg/day reduces fracture risk and improves BMD across osteoporosis types, with benefits persisting after treatment cessation; generally well tolerated but costly.

assessment.subject: degarelix (GnRH antagonist)
assessment.claim_summary: Review: in randomized phase II/III trials degarelix gave rapid, sustained testosterone and PSA suppression, noninferior to leuprolide but faster (castrate testosterone by day 3 vs day 28); generally well tolerated.
assessment.magnitude: castrate testosterone by day 3 (degarelix) vs day 28 (leuprolide)

assessment.subject: icatibant (bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist)
assessment.claim_summary: Review: subcutaneous icatibant 30 mg missed its primary endpoint (time to symptom relief) vs placebo in FAST-1 but was positive on secondary endpoints, and was significantly faster than tranexamic acid in FAST-2; well tolerated.
assessment.magnitude: median 0.6-1.0 h to first symptom improvement (laryngeal)

assessment.subject: icatibant (Firazyr, HOE 140)
assessment.claim_summary: Review concluding icatibant, a selective B2 bradykinin receptor antagonist approved by the EMEA, provided rapid, stable relief in phase III trials and is a new, safe and effective treatment for acute hereditary angioedema attacks.

assessment.subject: exenatide (exendin-4, GLP-1 agonist)
assessment.claim_summary: Review: exenatide, a GLP-1 receptor agonist, is consistently associated with weight loss in clinical trials, but evidence on the mechanism (reduced energy intake vs increased expenditure) is inconsistent and unresolved.
